{{Quote|Few Rebels could imagine that the source of this new delicacy was, in fact, the squat, ugly gornt, an omnivore native to the planet Hethar.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
'''Hethar''' was a [[Forest/Legends|forested]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Diet/Legends|omnivores]] known as [[Gornt/Legends|gornts]], whose [[Foodstuff/Legends|meat]] was a staple in the diet of the local [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]]. Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Annexation of Hethar|annexed]] the planet and instituted a gornt [[Reproduction/Legends|breeding]] and processing program, wherein [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Farmer/Legends|ranchers]] provided gornt meat as supplies for the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].

Over the following [[Standard year/Legends|years]], gornt breeding on Hethar began to face problems related to the creatures' reproduction, drawing Imperial [[Geneticist/Legends|geneticists]] to visit the planet in an attempt to solve the difficulties. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] team on Hethar encountered a pack of local [[shredder bat]]s that were eventually repelled via the use of the [[excluder]] device.

==Description==
{{Quote|This delicate reproductive balance has prevented the omnivorous gornt from stripping the forests bare ''[&hellip;]''|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
Hethar was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Creatures" /> located in the [[Hethar system/Legends|Hethar system]], a part of the [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]] in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA Hethar" /> The planet's surface featured [[Forest/Legends|forests]] in which [[Tree/Legends|trees]]<ref name="Creatures" /> and [[Color/Legends|brown]]-colored [[Bush/Legends|bushes]] grew.<ref name="DB">{{DB|creature|gornt|gornt}}</ref> Hethar was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Gornt/Legends|gornt]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Limb/Legends|quadrupedal]] [[Diet/Legends|omnivore]]. The delicate nature of the gornt [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] cycle prevented the creatures from stripping their homeworld's forests bare.<ref name="Creatures" />

The [[shredder bat]],<ref name="Gundark" /> a species of flying predator that had originally been encountered on<ref name="Creatures" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] planet<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Atrisia/Legends|Atrisia]] and had eventually spread to more than a thousand other worlds,<ref name="Creatures" /> was also found on Hethar.<ref name="Gundark" /> In addition, the planet's biosphere included a life-form that had a shell as part of its organism.<ref name="Creatures" />

==History==
{{Quote|We only had to use an excluder once, but boy, were we sure glad we brought on ''[sic]'' with us. We had gotten stuck on Hethar, checking out a small Imperial contingent there.|Homack, ''Gundark's Gear Datalog''|<ref name="Gundark" />}}
The gornt, a creature native to Hethar,<ref name="Creatures" /> was already known off-world<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|48|life/13321_1.html|Holo Critics Preemptively Bemoan Summer Season}}</ref> by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="22 BBY">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|48|life/13321_1.html|Holo Critics Preemptively Bemoan Summer Season}}, which mentions the [[Gornt/Legends|gornt]], is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] 13:3:21, which corresponds to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Annexation of Hethar|annexed]] the planet during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="DB" /> shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="CSWE Hethar">{{CSWECite|II|37|Hethar}}</ref> The local [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] offered the Imperial suppliers a staple of their own [[Foodstuff/Legends|diet]]: gornt meat. Due to the good qualities of the meat, the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] rapidly established a gornt breeding and processing program. Due to deals made by several [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] entrepreneurs, gornt [[Farm/Legends|ranches]] were established on Hethar and other planets.<ref name="Creatures" />

[[File:Gornt-DB.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The gornt was native to Hethar, where it was bred in ranches.]]
For [[Standard year/Legends|years]], wild gornts were rounded up, fattened, and bred to provide food for [[Navy/Legends|naval]] supplies. Eventually, however, due to factors that included forced breeding, overly rapid harvesting, changed diet, the use of fertility-modifying chemical treatments, and [[Bioengineering/Legends|tampering]] with the gornts' [[Gene/Legends|genetic]] code, the creatures' breeding cycle began to change, leading to a steady decrease in the number and quality of the herds kept on Hethar. Drawn to the challenge, Imperial [[Geneticist/Legends|geneticists]] traveled to the planet in order to attempt to find a solution to the gornt fertility problems. During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the Empire, the gornts of Hethar were given an entry in a [[Holo-brochure|holobrochure]] for the [[Tagge Holographic Museum]] of<ref name="Creatures" /> the planet<ref name="CSWE Chandrila">{{CSWECite|I|119|Chandrila}}</ref> [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]].<ref name="Creatures" />

At some point during the Galactic Civil War, a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] team including [[Homack]] became stuck on Hethar while [[Mission to Hethar|carrying out]] [[Scout/Legends|reconnaissance]] of a small Imperial contingent on the planet. One [[Standard day/Legends|night]], four Rebels, including Homack, on guard duty encountered a pack of shredder [[Bat/Legends|bats]]. Wary of using [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] to repel the creatures lest they be discovered by the Imperials, the Rebels stunned the creatures using the sonic animal repellent device known as the [[excluder]]. On the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] [[9 ABY/Legends|45:2:3:47]], Homack mentioned the incident on Hethar in the illegal database ''[[Gundark's Gear Datalog]]''.<ref name="Gundark" /> Hethar fell within the borders of the [[Pentastar Alignment]] between [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]]<ref name="TEA Hethar" /> and was situated in the [[Imperial Space|territory]] under the control of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] between 12 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]] and [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|When the Empire annexed Hethar, the local colonists offered a staple of their own diets to Imperial suppliers.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
Hethar had already been colonized by the [[Time/Legends|time]] the planet was annexed by the Galactic Empire. During the Empire's reign, Hethar was also home to wealthy Sullustan gornt ranchers and was occasionally visited by Imperial geneticists.<ref name="Creatures" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hethar was first mentioned in the [[1994]] sourcebook ''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]'', published by [[West End Games]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The section of the book mentioning the planet was authored by [[Phil Brucato]] and illustrated by [[Mike Vilardi]].<ref name="Creatures" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Hethar [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet Hethar, in grid square L-5.<ref name="TEA Hethar" />
